description: Guide a student to build a futures backtest engine with realistic execution simulation for a BTCUSDT breakout strategy, including slippage, maker versus taker fees, and funding-rate accounting.

student_openings.beginner_no_finance: I built a simple backtester but someone told me I'm ignoring trading fees and slippage. What are those and how do I add them?
student_openings.intermediate_developer: I need to add realistic execution simulation to my futures backtester: slippage, maker and taker fees, and funding rates. How should I structure the fill model?
student_openings.advanced_quant: I'm building a futures backtest engine with a full execution simulator: volume-aware slippage, maker/taker fee differentiation, and 8-hour funding-rate accounting. I want to decompose PnL into alpha, execution cost, and carry components. What's the architecture?

ground_truth.expected_outcome: Student produces a backtest system where (1) the engine has a configurable fill model with slippage, (2) fees are modeled with separate maker and taker rates, (3) funding-rate payments are deducted or credited every 8 hours for open positions, (4) the strategy implements a breakout system, and (5) the system runs and reports gross versus net performance, showing the impact of each cost component separately. Because this is a hard realism task, the run should leave concrete execution and cost-accounting artifacts such as trade logs or structured cost breakdowns.
required_capabilities: Build a fill or execution simulator with configurable slippage
Model maker and taker fee differentiation
Account for funding-rate payments on open futures positions
Break down performance into gross, net-of-fees, and net-of-fees-and-funding components
Explain why execution simulation matters for strategy viability
